searchText: Seeing as our testnet deposit contracts are likely to have an `owner` address for refunds, perhaps we could configure these two lines (link below) to permit `owner` to provide zero eth but still be assigned `MIN_DEPOSIT_AMOUNT` in the deposit log. That is, allow free deposits for the `owner` on testnet deposit contracts. https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/03fb0979485a204890053ae0b5dcbbe06c7f1f5c/deposit_contract/contracts/validator_registration.v.py#L75-L76 <@361447803194441738> I'd be wary of making changes to the deposit function's logic. In this case, you'd have to tweak deposit data to provide a false value of Ether and that could cause knock-on problems. And if you have a drain function you can obtain the Ether back very simply anyway with a separate call so nothing is lost pretty sure we have enough test ether to not need refunding though 😄 To be clear, I’m only taking about testnet contracts. I certainly wouldn’t suggest this for mainnet. It seems a trivial to change to me. There’s no actual need for the Eth to be in the contract. It's useful for testing deposit tooling, though. Leaving the `deposit()` function as will be on mainnet makes the testing more real-world, and given it's just gETH I don't see the problem of using it (and returning it if required with a drain) I think you’re taking about real-world testing and I’m talking about edge-case testing We already have several deposit contracts deployed that we use for testing. Making these as far-out as we can is very useful for unit testing. Yeah, I'm very much thinking about the tooling and real-world usage
